summary: 1938 steel K-brace fire tower on Grassy Mountain, Murray County, Georgia, in the Chattahoochee National Forest; NHLR-registered 2007; still standing but closed to climbing.

facts.design: 50-foot steel K-brace tower with an all-metal CL-100 series live-in cab; the NHLR gives the cab as 14 by 14 feet

access.note: Tower is fenced off and closed to climbing; the trail and summit clearing are open, per a trail guide. No public climb is described in any source read.

visit.trail_note: About four and a half miles round trip from Lake Conasauga, the highest lake in Georgia. The Lake Conasauga road closes from December 29 until March 1.

events.note: Build year per the NHLR. No source gives a reason for the tower or a builder.
Registered July 26, 2007; nominated by John Mayer
2014 trail report: top of tower locked off and the forest road leading to it closed. Closure dates not found.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR gives 3,511 ft (1,070 m) for the registered coordinates. A Georgia tower list and a trail guide give 3,694 ft. The record has no elevation field, so the story reports both figures and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: No staffing, fire history, or rental information in any source read. Elevation sources disagree (3,511 ft NHLR vs 3,694 ft list and trail guide); the record's elevation_m 1070.2 follows the NHLR. Access rests on an undated trail guide and a 2014 trail report, so recheck before giving visit advice. Do not confuse with us-ga-glassy-mountain (the NHLR itself warns of this). A Forest Lookouts page mentions an August 1949 National Archives photo; that photo page was not read, so none is listed under photos.
